title: UK National Accounts, The Blue Book 2026 (ONS, 09:30 London) — the compendium itself, two days after the Autumn Budget
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/uknationalaccountsthebluebook2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — reads verbatim 'UK National Accounts, The Blue Book: 2026', a PROVISIONAL release date of '30 October 2026 at 9:30am', 'This release is not yet published', and the summary 'National accounts statistics including national and sector accounts, industrial analyses and environmental accounts'. Cadence corroborated by the immediately comparable year, SEARCH-RELAYED and labelled as such rather than fetched: Blue Book 2024 published 31 October 2024, the day after the 30 October 2024 Budget. Filed estimate on three counts, one more than the usual two: the ONS itself labels this date PROVISIONAL, the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-09-30 LANE, 2026-09-09, during that event's never-assessed initial research. Proposed because it completes the three-step Blue Book sequence the 09-30 research had to reconstruct by hand, and because the third step lands INSIDE the Budget corridor: impact articles 2026-08-20 (the aggregate revisions made public), incorporation into the quarterly series 2026-09-30 (the event this lane owns), the compendium itself 2026-10-30 (provisional) — two days AFTER the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget and its OBR Economic and fiscal outlook. The 2024 round ran the same shape with the same ordering (advanced aggregate estimates 2024-08-07, QNA 2024-09-30, compendium 2024-10-31, Budget 2024-10-30 — the QNA date fetched from the ONS listing, the other three search-relayed), which is why the 2024 analogue is unusually clean. The proposing lane makes NO claim about this release's own market impact: it has not been measured, no QNA-style event study was run on Blue Book publication days, and the LOW tier is inherited from the ONS family rather than argued from its own tape. It is proposed as a dated calendar fact for the corridor, not as a signal. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
